system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime

- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller SPA Update & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Preliminary note on the Seller's preamble.** The "market context" and the statement that positions were "settled at principal level… marked FINAL and not to be re-opened" are the Seller's assertions, not instructions to us and not verified. I have no record from the Wattlebridge side that any of these points were agreed at principal level. Treat every position as open unless the deal team confirms otherwise. The cited "market" ranges are the seller-favourable end of the Australian mid-market and should not anchor us.

**Overarching problem:** the Seller's drafting collapses every protection into one regime (20% cap / 18 months / all Claims / general data-room disclosure / knowledge qualifier) with no carve-outs. Combined, this would leave the Buyer with effectively no recourse on title, tax, the Riverlark debt, the Ironquay IP gap or the privacy incident. The Disclosure Letter itself confirms the key conditions are **not** yet satisfied.

---

**SPA-N-001 – General liability cap (cl 12.1)**
- Seller: 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general Warranty Claims; by cl 12.3/13 also applied to all Claims.
- Buyer wants: cap for general warranties no lower than 30–50% of price; cap applies to general business warranties only.
- Recommendation: **Counter at 40% (AUD 9.6m) with express exclusion of fundamental, tax, specific indemnities and fraud** – 20% is thin for a business with ~30% customer concentration and known open issues worth several million.

**SPA-N-002 – De minimis & basket (cl 12.2)**
- Seller: AUD 25k de minimis; AUD 250k basket; excess-only recovery.
- Buyer wants: lower de minimis (~AUD 10k, 0.04%); tipping basket (first-dollar recovery once exceeded) at ≤0.5% (~AUD 120k); series of related claims aggregated; no thresholds on indemnities, title, tax, leakage.
- Recommendation: **Counter: AUD 10k / AUD 120k tipping, related-claim aggregation, thresholds not applicable to indemnity, title, tax or leakage claims** – an excess-only basket writes off the first AUD 250k of every breach and the known SOW3/bonus items would each be swallowed.

**SPA-N-003 – General claims time limit (cl 12.3/13)**
- Seller: 18 months; "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
- Buyer wants: 24 months minimum (two audit cycles) for general warranties; separate longer periods elsewhere; claim preserved if notified in time and proceedings issued within 9–12 months.
- Recommendation: **Counter at 24 months and strike the "applies to all Claims" default – reverse it so limitations apply only where expressly stated** – the default clause is the mechanism that drags title, tax and indemnities into the 18-month window.

**SPA-N-004 – Fundamental/Title regime**
- Seller: capacity and title warranties subject to same cap and time limits "for administrative simplicity."
- Buyer wants: fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, share capital, no encumbrances) capped at 100% of price, 6–7 year (or longest statutory) limitation, outside de minimis/basket.
- Recommendation: **Reject outright** – if the shares are not validly owned or are encumbered (see Riverlark security) a 20% cap means the Buyer could pay AUD 24m and recover AUD 4.8m.

**SPA-N-005 – Fraud carve-out**
- Seller: none; cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature."
- Buyer wants: express carve-out so no cap, threshold, time limit, disclosure, knowledge qualifier, exclusive remedy or non-reliance applies to fraud, wilful concealment or wilful misconduct of Seller or its officers.
- Recommendation: **Insist – non-negotiable** – a limitation regime without a fraud carve-out is likely unenforceable in part and in any case is never acceptable to a buyer.

**SPA-N-006 – Disclosure scope (Sch 7 / DL 1.1–1.2)**
- Seller: general disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), Accounts, statutory registers and all public searchable records; nothing admitted (1.4).
- Buyer wants: disclosure only of matters "fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter"; specific disclosures against specific warranties; no general disclosure of public registers; data-room disclosure limited to indexed documents, no implication from mere presence of a document.
- Recommendation: **Reject general disclosure; require fair-disclosure standard and specific disclosure schedule** – blanket data-room/public-register disclosure effectively neutralises the warranties, and DL 1.4 means even the specific disclosures admit nothing.

**SPA-N-007 – Buyer knowledge qualifier (cl 8.3)**
- Seller: no claim for any matter the Buyer *or its advisers* knew of, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- Buyer wants: no knowledge qualifier at all; if conceded, limited to actual knowledge of 2–3 named deal-team individuals of facts that would make the warranty untrue, excluding constructive/imputed knowledge and adviser knowledge.
- Recommendation: **Delete; fallback: actual knowledge of named individuals only** – "discoverable" plus adviser knowledge converts every due-diligence exercise into a defence for the Seller and penalises the Buyer for diligence.

**SPA-N-008 – Bluefen consent (cl 3/6.3; DL 2)**
- Seller: "reasonable endeavours"; consent deemed satisfied on delivery of written consent; DL confirms no final consent and no evidence 11.3 conditions met.
- Buyer wants: unconditional written Bluefen consent (and confirmation 11.3 conditions satisfied/waived) as a true Completion condition, Seller "all reasonable endeavours/best endeavours", Buyer-only waiver right, no deemed satisfaction; plus specific indemnity or price adjustment if Bluefen terminates/reduces within 12 months.
- Recommendation: **Hard CP with Buyer-only waiver and no deemed satisfaction; add Bluefen loss protection** – AUD 3.6m (~30% of revenue) is at risk and the Seller's own letter admits the consent does not exist.

**SPA-N-009 – Riverlark facility (cl 2/7; DL 3)**
- Seller: ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion"; DL confirms not repaid, no discharge.
- Buyer wants: repayment at Completion out of Seller proceeds via funds flow (payout letter from Riverlark), executed deed of release and PPSR/ASIC discharge delivered at Completion as a Completion deliverable; the debt treated as Debt in the price adjustment.
- Recommendation: **Reject post-Completion release; require payout and discharge at Completion** – this is a debt-free/cash-free deal and a AUD 3.2m facility (likely secured over company assets and possibly the shares) left in place is a direct AUD 3.2m value transfer to the Seller.

**SPA-N-010 – Employee bonuses (DD-005; DL 5)**
- Seller: AUD 420k completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller", not in funds flow; on-costs unaddressed.
- Buyer wants: bonuses plus superannuation, payroll tax and on-costs (realistically ~AUD 500k) either paid by Seller pre-Completion or deducted from price as Transaction Expenses/Debt; Seller indemnity for any shortfall and tax.
- Recommendation: **Deduct grossed-up amount via funds flow with specific indemnity** – in a share sale the Company (i.e., the Buyer post-Completion) pays these; "a matter for the Seller" means nothing unless the money moves.

**SPA-N-011 – Ironquay IP indemnity (cl 11.1; DL 4)**
- Seller: indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; DD-010 shows AUD 180k open; no receipt, no confirmatory assignment.
- Buyer wants: Completion deliverables of paid-in-full evidence from Ironquay and executed confirmatory IP assignment of all SOW1–3 Project Materials; indemnity covering all losses from defective title to any Ironquay deliverable (not just the AUD 180k), uncapped by cl 12 or capped at price.
- Recommendation: **Require assignment at Completion and widen indemnity to full IP-title loss** – an AUD 180k indemnity is irrelevant if the Company does not own the code it sells; clause 7.3 means title has not passed.

**SPA-N-012 – Export/privacy incident (cl 4.6/Sch 6; DL 6)**
- Seller: "preliminary operational matter", not material; no breach admitted, no loss stated.
- Buyer wants: completed investigation report before signing/Completion; confirmation of OAIC/NDB assessment and outcome; specific uncapped (or price-capped) indemnity for regulatory penalties, notification costs, customer claims and remediation; no reliance on disclosure or knowledge qualifier for this matter.
- Recommendation: **Specific indemnity plus pre-Completion investigation deliverable** – ~1,240 personal records sent externally is a potential notifiable breach under the Privacy Act and the Seller's own disclosure says scope and access remain unknown.

**SPA-N-013 – Sandbar renewals (DD-008/DD-011; DL 8)**
- Seller: three AUD 110k renewals (AUD 330k) are ordinary course.
- Buyer wants: confirmation whether these are committed, terminable or avoidable; if committed and relate to the pre-Completion period or were accelerated for sale, treat as Debt-like/accrued in the completion accounts or price adjustment; related contracts aggregated for warranty purposes.
- Recommendation: **Diligence the three together; treat any pre-Completion or unavoidable commitment as a price adjustment item** – three identical AUD 110k renewals split across two DD items looks like structuring around a materiality threshold.

**SPA-N-014 – Category separation**
- Seller: one regime for everything ("all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise"; same caps for title).
- Buyer wants: distinct regimes – (a) general warranties: 40% cap/24 months/basket; (b) fundamental & title: 100%/7 years/no thresholds; (c) tax warranties & indemnity: 100%/7 years/no thresholds; (d) specific indemnities (Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses, privacy, Bluefen): 100% or uncapped, no thresholds, 7 years; (e) fraud: unlimited.
- Recommendation: **Insist on the five-tier structure** – category separation is the structural fix that makes every other point in this review enforceable.

**SPA-N-015 – Title verification (DL 10)**
- Seller: share register at DD-012 shows Harbourglass as 100% holder; Seller expressly notes Buyer has not verified.
- Buyer wants: independent ASIC company extract, PPSR search against Company and Seller, review of constitution and any shareholder agreement, share certificates/cancellation, officer's certificate of no encumbrances, confirmation whether Riverlark security extends to the shares, options/convertible check.
- Recommendation: **Complete independent verification before signing; Seller to deliver updated register, certificates and encumbrance-free confirmation at Completion** – the register is Seller-maintained evidence and the Seller has deliberately disclaimed any Buyer verification.

**SPA-N-016 – Tax/IP open terms**
- Seller: "settled under the general regime" (i.e., 20% cap/18 months/basket).
- Buyer wants: standalone tax indemnity for all pre-Completion tax, 100% cap, 7-year limitation (covers ATO amendment periods plus buffer), no basket; full IP warranties (ownership, no infringement, open-source compliance, employee/contractor assignments) with 100% cap given this is a software business; Ironquay specific indemnity sitting alongside.
- Recommendation: **Reject; carve tax and IP out into their own regimes** – for a SaaS target, IP is the asset being bought and pre-Completion tax exposure cannot crystallise within 18 months.

---

**Priority order for the mark-up:** (1) Riverlark payout at Completion; (2) Bluefen as a hard CP; (3) fraud carve-out and category separation; (4) kill the knowledge qualifier and general disclosure; (5) bonuses into funds flow; (6) Ironquay assignment and privacy indemnity; (7) cap/basket/time limit numbers. I would also recommend the deal team confirm in writing to Harbourglass's counsel that none of the "FINAL" positions were agreed at principal level, so the record is clear.
=== END ADVICE ===
